sizeReason: Ana, Ben and Chloe have 60 hours across 14 days, which fits a short, full plan. Their beginner skills and free budget call for one simple website, not microservices and Kubernetes. Passwords need secure hashing and reset links. The expected photos total about 10 GB and cannot fit in a 500 MB database; photo storage and limits need a workable plan.

parts.summary: Build a warm family cookbook where about 60 classmates and their families can share recipes, photos and comments.
parts.details: The graded version is due on day 14. Ana has Python basics, Ben knows HTML/CSS, and Chloe knows some JavaScript. Each has 20 hours. Plan 14 hours per person and keep 6 hours each for surprises: 42 planned hours and an 18-hour buffer. The 42 hours include 8 hours of Django learning, interface work, security and testing. Django is a Python toolkit for building websites. Everything must be free. No outside rules were supplied; check school hosting and privacy requirements before collecting real family data. Success means an approved member can log in, publish a recipe with up to five photos, and receive a comment.

parts.summary: Keep email accounts, recipes with up to five photos, and comments. Delay search, favourites and optional upload effects.
parts.details:
Day-one acceptance:
- A person signs up with email and password, sees an approval message, and can log in after an administrator confirms membership. Wrong passwords fail.
- Only approved members can read recipes, comments and photo files.
- A member publishes a title, ingredients, steps and zero to five photos. The recipe remains after reloading. A sixth photo is refused.
- Comments remain after reloading. Members cannot change someone else's content.
- Passwords use Argon2, a slow one-way password check. Existing passwords cannot be retrieved or emailed.
- A member can follow the documented recovery process: contact the administrator, pass an identity check, and receive a temporary reset link through an existing trusted contact route.

By day 2, agree fields and prove free hosting, private photo access and storage limits. By day 3, demonstrate login. By day 5, demonstrate five-photo submission. By day 7, show signup through approval, posting and commenting. Days 8–14 are for checks, repairs and presentation.

If work slips, drop previews, per-photo progress and separate retries first; these are not scheduled. Then simplify visual polish. Keep five-photo submission unless the team explicitly accepts a smaller release. Never cut password or access protection.

options.bad: Consumes checking time and adds storage demands.

parts.summary: Use one Django application, HTML/CSS pages and SQLite, a database stored in one file. Try PythonAnywhere's free plan by day 2.
parts.details:
Ana owns Python server work. Ben builds templates and styles. Chloe handles deployment and checking, without being assigned Python photo implementation. Include 8 learning hours: Ana 4, Ben 2 and Chloe 2. Each person's full planned share is 14 hours, leaving 6 hours each for surprises before day 14.

Use email login and Django's existing account machinery. Install django[argon2], put django.contrib.auth.hashers.Argon2PasswordHasher first in PASSWORD_HASHERS, and retain supported fallback hashers. Verify that new and reset passwords use Argon2id, the selected Argon2 variant. [Django password setup](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/topics/auth/passwords/)

Use administrator-approved signup and identity-checked, administrator-assisted reset-link delivery. This avoids custom invitation handling and a required email provider. Keep search, favourites and photo previews for later. Drop microservices, Docker, Kubernetes and a separate front-end project.

PythonAnywhere currently lists one web app, one worker, 512 MiB of disk and a one-month app expiry. New free accounts do not include scheduled tasks. Chloe must test deployment, secure photo access and actual disk use by day 2; use manual backups and renewal reminders. [Free-plan limits](https://help.pythonanywhere.com/pages/FreeAccountsFeatures)

parts.summary: Keep accounts, recipes, comments and photos together. Use ordinary page forms and one deployment.
parts.details:
The browser submits a recipe and up to five photos together. Django checks membership, ownership and input. Ana validates all photos before publishing the recipe, saves reduced files and cleans up temporary files on failure. No independent uploads or saved partial upload state are required.

Require approved membership for recipe pages, comments and every photo request. Keep photo files outside public static directories and serve them through a checked application route. Reuse Django's administrator interface for approvals and content removal; do not build a moderator dashboard.

Keep five-photo limits, text limits and ownership decisions in small pure functions: values go in, answers come out. Views handle requests, database calls and file operations around them. Use accounts/, recipes/, templates/ and static/. Split files before about 400 lines. Reuse helpers and explain only reasons or traps in comments.

Test rules without a database or network. Integration checks then cover signup, approval, login, posting, comments, forbidden changes, bad uploads and restoration. All work uses the shared task IDs below; security and interface checks are included, not additional estimates.

parts.summary: Store account and recipe records in SQLite, and reduced photos as private files. The original photos would need about 10 GB.
parts.details:
Records: User (unique login email, display name, protected password, approval status), Recipe (author, title, ingredients, steps), Photo (recipe, path, order, bytes), Comment (recipe, author, text, date). Decide the email-based user model before the first database setup. Hide email addresses from classmates.

Accept zero to five JPEG/PNG photos per recipe. Limit each incoming file to 5 MB and 20 megapixels, meaning 20 million pixels. Use an image library to decode, resize and re-save each image without location metadata. Limit stored output to 100 KB; reject it with a clear message if acceptable quality cannot fit. Discard originals.

At that output limit, 2,000 images need at most 200 MB. This is a photo-size calculation, not a capacity promise. Reserve 50 MB for records and at least 50 MB of free disk for temporary work. Measure application and package use on day 2. Set the photo budget to the smaller of 200 MB and the remaining safe allowance. Check total usage before saving; prevent simultaneous requests from exceeding the allowance.

Each active day, pause writes and copy the database and photo files together to a private computer. Keep three backup copies off the host, test restoration before grading, and agree who deletes hosted data and backups afterward. Keep secrets outside source control.

parts.summary: Use Argon2 password protection, administrator-approved membership and private photo access. Fit these into the same 42-hour schedule.
parts.details:
Ana's Python basics suit server work, Ben's HTML/CSS suits account forms, and Chloe's JavaScript experience supports checking browser flows. Each has 20 hours; plan 14 and reserve 6. The security work below is included in the shared tasks, not an extra 16 hours. The budget is free and the deadline is day 14.

Use Argon2, a slow one-way password check. Ana installs django[argon2] and places Argon2PasswordHasher first in PASSWORD_HASHERS during A2. Chloe checks new and reset passwords use Argon2id during C4. [Django password configuration](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/topics/auth/passwords/)

New signups remain inactive until an administrator confirms the person belongs to the class or an intended family through an existing trusted contact. Use Django's administrator interface. Pending accounts cannot read pages or download photos. Do not build invitation tokens, custom moderator roles or per-account photo quotas for day one. The administrator can remove inappropriate content using existing tools.

Recovery starts with 'Forgot password?' and a page explaining whom to contact. The administrator verifies the person in person or through a previously established school/family contact, then generates a standard Django reset link and sends it privately through that route. Set a one-hour expiry. Never accept a newly supplied contact address as proof of identity. Do not disclose the existing password, set a shared temporary password or record reset links in logs. Test successful reset, expiry and reuse before real signup.

Check approved membership on every recipe, comment and photo request. Check ownership before member changes. Render recipe and comment text as text, not executable markup. Keep Django's form protections against forged requests enabled. Configure temporary login-attempt limits using an established compatible component, including the administrator login; test them in C4.

Ana validates and re-saves photos in A4. Chloe checks HTTPS, which encrypts traffic, private file placement, secrets and production settings in C2. If free hosting cannot support these controls, use fictional accounts in a local demonstration until hosting is resolved. Confirm school privacy requirements before collecting family data.

parts.summary: Make a warm family cookbook with cream backgrounds, dark text, muted terracotta buttons and generous recipe photos. Support phones and laptops.
parts.details:
Build five screen groups: recipe list, recipe detail with comments, add/edit recipe, signup/login, and recovery. Reuse the account layout for approval and recovery messages.

Private entry is login → recipe list → recipe detail → read or comment. A new member follows signup → 'Your account is waiting for approval' → administrator approval → login. Explain that recipes and photos are available only after approval. There are no invitation links. Use a general login error with a pointer to approval help, so the page does not reveal whether another person's email is registered.

Posting is login → fill one grouped form → publish. Ask for title, ingredients, steps and zero to five photos. Explain accepted formats and size limits before the file picker. Day one has no previews, per-photo progress, separate retries or preserved successful uploads. Chloe is assigned deployment and testing, not this optional JavaScript.

Submit the form once. Show 'Uploading your recipe. Please wait.' without claiming a percentage. On server validation errors, preserve recipe text, explain the problem and ask the person to select photos again; browsers do not refill file inputs. On an uncertain connection failure, tell the person to check the recipe list before retrying, because the save may have succeeded. Do not promise text recovery after a lost connection; advise keeping a copy of long recipes.

Recovery text: 'Forgot your password? Contact the cookbook administrator using the contact shown here. After checking who you are, they will send a private link so you can choose a new password. We cannot retrieve your old password.' Insert a real contact before launch. A reset page explains that links expire after one hour; an expired or used link sends the person back to the recovery instructions.

Use visible labels, readable 18px body text, strong contrast, keyboard focus and errors linked to their fields. Reuse one header, page container, button style and form layout. Ben owns 12 interface hours within his 14 planned hours; his other 2 hours are template learning. Ana connects the server forms. Chloe checks complete flows within her existing tasks. Use system fonts and CSS, with no paid assets, for the day-14 deadline.

problems.problem: The 42-hour plan does not account for the 8 hours of Django learning. Adding those hours leaves only 10 hours for surprises, below the required 18-hour buffer.
problems.fix: Include learning in the task estimates and reduce other work until planned work totals at most 42 hours. Keep each person's planned share at or below 14 hours.

problems.problem: The 38 hours of architecture tasks have no named owners or clear overlap with the other tasks. Adding the designer's 12 hours already exceeds the 42-hour work allowance, before any extra security work.
problems.fix: Map these tasks into one shared 42-hour schedule. Name Ana, Ben or Chloe as the sole owner of each task, and explicitly include overlapping security and interface work only once.

problems.problem: Chloe has some JavaScript experience, but gets only four hours to implement server-side photo validation, resizing, storage and limits. The plan does not allow for learning Python or integrating this work with Django.
problems.fix: Assign Python photo handling to Ana and previews to Chloe, or explicitly budget Chloe's Python and Django learning. Rebalance the remaining work within each person's hours.

problems.problem: Single-use email invitations, moderator permissions and account quotas add required work beyond the basic recipe website. The security tasks have no named owners, and their inclusion in the 42-hour plan is unclear.
problems.fix: Assign each task to a teammate and include it in the shared estimates. Compare custom invitations with a simpler administrator-approved membership process, then choose an option that fits the hours.

problems.problem: Per-photo progress, separate retries and keeping successful uploads require more upload state and JavaScript than the proposed ordinary Django form. That work has no explicit estimate or owner.
problems.fix: Compare a single form submission with a clear waiting message and retry against independent photo uploads. Choose the simpler form for day one unless Chloe's implementation and testing time fits the shared budget.

problems.problem: The account plan relies on Django's default password protection without explicitly choosing one of the required slow hashes. It also differs from the explicit Argon2 configuration in the security requirements.
problems.fix: Specify Argon2 as the preferred password hasher, include its dependency and configuration in the account task, and verify that new accounts use it.

problems.problem: The entry path starts with browsing and ordinary signup, but the selected security approach requires membership before reading recipes or photos. There is no invitation entry or invalid-invitation state.
problems.fix: Start the private browsing path with login. Reuse the account layout for invitation signup and explain what happens when an invitation is missing, expired or already used.

problems.problem: The fallback cuts the five-photo requirement before explicitly optional preview, upload-progress and retry features. This can break a day-one requirement while retaining interface extras.
problems.fix: Cut advanced upload feedback and previews before reducing the photo count. Keep five-photo submission unless the team explicitly accepts a smaller release.

problems.problem: Password recovery has no defined user path when free email delivery is unavailable. A local demonstration is a fallback for hosting, but does not explain what a member should do after forgetting a password.
problems.fix: Compare reset-link delivery with a documented administrator-assisted identity check. Choose and test one before inviting real users, and provide matching recovery text.

sections.summary: A private class cookbook, ready in 14 days.
sections.details: Ana knows basic Python, Ben HTML/CSS, and Chloe some JavaScript. Each has 20 hours: 14 planned and six reserved for fixes. Everything must be free. No AI. Confirm school requirements before collecting accounts or photos.

sections.summary: Size the first release to 60 hours
sections.details: Choose accounts, recipes, five photos and comments: achievable but tight. Adding search and favourites offers more features but exceeds available time. Save week 2 for checks, fixes and grading.

Choose Django, a Python website toolkit: existing account tools help Ana, though learning takes time. Separate services allow independent updates but overwhelm 60 hours. Use ordinary pages and SQLite, a single-file database. Chloe checks hosting by day 2.

Choose administrator-approved signup: simple and private, but members wait. Invitations reduce waiting but add delivery work. Check membership for content and photos; check ownership before changes. Keep rules in pure functions, separate from storage. Reuse helpers; split files near 400 lines.

Choose database records plus private photo files: simple, but disk space is shared. Hosted file storage adds capacity but setup work. Keep photo paths with records. Allow five JPEG/PNG photos, each ≤5 MB and ≤20 megapixels. Re-save without location details to ≤100 KB; enforce measured storage limits.

Choose Django with Argon2id hashes, one-way password checks: supports email login but needs setup. School login reduces password work, but family access is unknown. Require HTTPS encrypted connections, login-attempt limits and form protections. Hide emails, protect photo access, show comments as text and keep secrets outside shared code.

sections.summary: Warm cream pages, dark text and terracotta buttons.
sections.details: Choose one grouped recipe form: easier for Ben, but more scrolling. Staged forms shorten screens but add work. Choose photos submitted together: less code, but failures require reselection. Separate uploads improve retries but exceed Chloe's time. Cover lists, recipes, posting, accounts and recovery. Preserve text after errors; support phones and keyboards.

Choose administrator-assisted reset links: no email provider, but identity checks take time. Automatic email is quicker for members but adds delivery setup. Verify through an existing trusted contact route. Links expire after one hour and work once. Show the administrator's contact on recovery and approval pages.

sections.summary: Prove hosting early; finish the complete journey by day 7.
sections.details: Ana owns application rules, Ben pages, Chloe delivery and checks. Eight learning hours are included. Pause changes while copying records and photos together; keep three private copies off the host and test restoration. Cut effects and polish first; preserve security and checking time.

pushBacks.idea: Store readable passwords and email them back.
pushBacks.problem: Database or mailbox leaks expose usable passwords.
pushBacks.better: Store Argon2id hashes; provide identity-checked reset links.

pushBacks.problem: Several deployments exceed this team's skills and time.
pushBacks.better: Use one Django application with clear folders.

pushBacks.idea: Put 2,000 original 5 MB photos in a 500 MB database.
pushBacks.problem: 10,000 MB is twenty times the allowance.
pushBacks.better: Reduce private files and measure capacity; 200 MB of reduced photos still needs proven hosting.

pushBacks.idea: Reduce photo count while keeping advanced upload feedback.
pushBacks.problem: Optional effects displace a required feature.
pushBacks.better: Keep five photos; defer previews and separate retries.

choices.question: What hosting does grading require?
options: Local demonstration: easiest within 60 hours, but no shared online access; needs grading permission.
School hosting: potentially simpler, but availability needs confirming.
Public hosting: remote access, but free capacity needs proving.

choices.question: Does 60 include families, and when are 2,000 photos expected?
options: Families included, photos later: manageable launch, but expansion remains.
Families additional or photos immediate: broader participation, but greater capacity risk.

choices.question: Who approves accounts and verifies recovery through trusted contacts?
options: School adult: continuity, but availability needs agreement.
Named teammate: quick coordination, but uses limited hours.

choices.question: Will children participate, and what school privacy, device or access requirements apply?
options: Requirements known: clearer scope, but may add work; share them.
Unknown: confirm before signup; avoids rework, but may delay launch.

choices.question: What happens after grading?
options: Delete on an agreed date: less upkeep, but access ends.
Name a caretaker: continued access, but ongoing hosting and backup work.

decision.title: Password protection

options.name: Django login with Argon2
options.good: Meets email/password login without inventing password handling.
options.bad: Needs an added dependency, configuration and attempt limits.
options.fit: Included in Ana's A2 and Chloe's C4.

options.name: School-managed login
options.good: The school handles password protection and recovery.
options.bad: Availability and access for families are unknown.
options.fit: Only useful if an existing school service supports everyone and the login requirement can change.

decision.why: It meets the brief and uses established tools. Explicit configuration avoids assuming the default is Argon2.

decision.title: Application structure

options.name: One Django application
options.good: Supplies account, form and administrator tools in one place.
options.bad: Requires learning Django.
options.fit: Uses Ana's Python and Ben's HTML/CSS, with 8 learning hours explicitly included.

options.name: One Flask application
options.good: Offers a small Python starting point.
options.bad: Requires joining more account and form components.
options.fit: Fits Ana's language knowledge but adds integration choices before day 14.

options.name: Separate services with Kubernetes
options.good: Allows separate deployment and scaling.
options.bad: Requires several deployments, service connections and cluster administration.
options.fit: No relevant experience is stated; it does not fit 60 total hours.

decision.why: The required work is ordinary accounts, forms and pages. Existing framework tools save setup work.

decision.title: Photo and record storage

options.name: SQLite and reduced private files on one host
options.good: Avoids a database server and a second storage service.
options.bad: Application files and photos share limited disk space.
options.fit: Preferred if Chloe proves capacity and private access within C2.

options.name: Database records and separate hosted photo storage
options.good: Can provide more photo capacity.
options.bad: Adds service setup, permissions and transfer limits.
options.fit: Consider later, or if the school provides a ready-to-use private service.

options.name: Original photos inside the 500 MB database
options.good: Records and files can be copied together.
options.bad: About 100 original photos fill the allowance before other data.
options.fit: Cannot support 2,000 originals on the stated budget.

decision.picked: SQLite and reduced private files on one host
decision.why: One storage location is easier to operate. The day-2 measurement sets the real capacity.

decision.title: Size the first release to 60 hours

options.name: Small complete release
options.good: Keeps all required activities and five-photo submission.
options.bad: Leaves search, favourites and upload extras for later.
options.fit: Uses 42 planned hours, including learning, with 18 hours reserved.

options.name: One-photo release
options.good: Reduces upload and layout work.
options.bad: Misses the requested five-photo requirement.
options.fit: Only an explicit team-approved scope change after optional features and polish have been cut.

options.name: Expanded release
options.good: Adds search, favourites and richer upload feedback.
options.bad: Consumes checking time and adds storage demands.
options.fit: Too large for three beginners, 14 days and a free-only budget.

decision.why: A working required flow matters more than extras. Learning and all implementation work must fit inside the same 42 hours.

decision.title: Private membership

options.name: Administrator-approved signup
options.good: Uses existing account activation controls and avoids invitation-token code.
options.bad: Members wait for approval and someone must verify them.
options.fit: The smallest private membership process for this 60-hour project.

options.name: Single-use email invitations
options.good: Allows approved recipients to join directly.
options.bad: Needs token creation, expiry, delivery, reuse checks and extra screens.
options.fit: Too much additional implementation for the 42-hour work allowance.

options.name: Public browsing and open signup
options.good: Makes joining immediate.
options.bad: Exposes family photos and increases unwanted posts.
options.fit: Adds ongoing moderation work without a named operator.

decision.why: It keeps recipes and photos private using existing administrator tools. No invitation links means no missing, expired or used invitation states to implement.

decision.title: Forgotten-password recovery

options.name: Administrator-assisted reset-link delivery
options.good: Works without a new email service and still lets the member choose the password.
options.bad: Requires a trusted identity check and an available administrator.
options.fit: Selected for day one; implementation is in A2, wording in B3 and checks in C4.

options.name: Automatic reset email
options.good: Members recover access without waiting for an administrator.
options.bad: Needs a permitted free sender, delivery checks and request limits.
options.fit: A later option if the school provides a working sender and time permits.

decision.why: Free email delivery is unproven. Name an administrator and test identity checks and link delivery before inviting real users.

decision.title: How people enter a recipe

options.name: One grouped form
options.good: Shows recipe details and photos together and needs fewer screens.
options.bad: Long recipes require scrolling on phones.
options.fit: Fits Ben's HTML/CSS and Ana's ordinary Django forms.

options.name: Step-by-step form
options.good: Shows fewer fields at once.
options.bad: Needs navigation, saved progress and more checking.
options.fit: Adds work beyond the 42-hour planned allowance.

decision.why: Clear groups keep the form understandable without extra browser state.

decision.title: Photo submission and feedback

options.name: One submission with a waiting message
options.good: Works with ordinary Django forms and keeps five-photo submission.
options.bad: A failed validation requires selecting photos again; there is no per-photo percentage.
options.fit: Included in Ben's B3, Ana's A4 and existing verification tasks.

options.name: Independent photo uploads
options.good: Can show individual progress, retry one photo and retain completed uploads.
options.bad: Needs upload identifiers, temporary storage cleanup and more JavaScript and testing.
options.fit: Does not fit Chloe's planned hours; defer until after grading.

decision.picked: One submission with a waiting message
decision.why: It preserves the required photo count while keeping implementation and failure states small.
